title: 2002 HMMT February Advanced Topics Problem 3
statement: How many four-digit numbers are there in which at least one digit occurs more than once?

solutions.text: 4464 . There are 9000 four-digit numbers altogether. If we consider how many four-digit numbers have all their digits distinct, there are 9 choices for the first digit (since we exclude leading zeroes), and then 9 remaining choices for the second digit, then 8 for the third, and 7 for the fourth, for a total of \(9 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7=4536\). Thus the remaining \(9000-4536=4464\) numbers have a repeated digit.
